data.narrative:
Quantum-Systems, a Series C defense and security company founded by Florian Seibel, carries a current post-money valuation of $8.0B following $1.2B in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 12 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies spanning both private and public markets, including comparables such as Neros ($2.5B, Series C), Saronic ($9.2B, Series D), and Helsing ($18.0B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $8.0B base, implies $13.6B. The peer-median approach, using a cohort of 12 defense and security companies (range: $300M–$18.0B), yields a median valuation of $1.8B. The divergence between these methods reflects wide dispersion within the peer set and stage-specific positioning uncertainty.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.5B to $15.6B, with a median of $7.7B. The current $8.0B valuation sits near the triangulated midpoint, suggesting reasonable baseline calibration. Key uncertainties include the appropriate peer comparator weight—whether to emphasize later-stage multiples (Helsing, Saronic) or exact-stage matches (Neros)—and whether stage-progression multipliers derived from broader venture datasets apply to defense-sector dynamics. The wide peer range ($300M–$18.0B) reflects meaningful dispersion in company maturity and market position within this sector.
